identification: Late 19th C Tasmanian two-door wardrobe, door panels (arched-top upper, rectangular lower) in figured birdseye/burr Huon pine, frame, stiles and plinth stained dark (probably Huon or pine under stain), plain plinth base, cornice/pelmet missing. Interior: plain pale backboards, hanging rail, five brass hooks with ceramic tips, one shelf over a bottom compartment. Long vertical split down the left door's meeting stile from the top. Faint stencil on lower right door panel, illegible at the 800x600 source size. H190 W121 D46. Estimate $150-250, current bid $70 (27 Nov).

viewing_check: Are the door panels solid birdseye huon or veneer? Is the frame huon under stain (scrape an inside edge)? How long and deep is the split in the left door stile, and does it go through? Read the stencil on the lower right panel. Check the top for screw holes where the cornice went (a replacement cornice is easy). Check for borer in the base and backboards, and measure.
